title: Event Pal for fetes · powered by AVA
intro: Event Pal for fetes. One system, from the drop to the morning after. Powered by AVA.

steps.title: The brief
steps.text: It starts with the brief. Fill it in, or send the PDF to AVA on Telegram, and she sets up a draft of your fete for you to check.

steps.title: AVA knows you
steps.text: Your Telegram's linked to your account, so AVA knows who you are. She only shows you your own fetes, and she checks with you before anything goes public.

steps.title: Locked down
steps.text: Your fete is locked down. No one sees your ticket sales or event information. Every login has its own role, every change is logged, and our codes are signed, so they can't be forged.

steps.title: The drop
steps.text: Approve it, and the fete goes live. The flyer, the tiers and the countdown are listed on AVA, and shared to your socials in one tap.

steps.title: Early bird
steps.text: Early bird opens first. When it sells out, the price moves to general by itself.

steps.title: Tiers and wristbands
steps.text: General, VIP and all-inclusive. Each tier gets its own colour, and its own lane at the gate. And its own wristband, if wristbands are used.

steps.title: Ticket outlets and your team
steps.text: Outlets sell from a sales page or a sales device. Scanning a ticket at the sale is what activates it. Every street promoter gets a code. So you see who sold what, in real time, and what each outlet owes you.

steps.title: Lost or stolen
steps.text: A ticket that was never sold won't open the gate. A lost one is blocked in seconds.

steps.title: AVA before the fete
steps.text: Fans ask AVA anything. What time it starts, which outlets still have tickets, and what's in the all-inclusive.

steps.title: The gates
steps.text: At the gate, scan, and they're in. Our codes can't be copied or edited, and a screenshot gets caught. You always know how many are inside, and how close you are to capacity.

steps.title: The bars
steps.text: Every bar runs on an Event Pal till. Your bars and outside bars, bottle bars and cocktail bars, all on one floor plan.

steps.title: All-inclusive
steps.text: All-inclusive guests tap their wristband to be served, if wristbands are used. No cash, no tokens, and the limits you set, per night or per hour.

steps.title: Bar sales in real time
steps.text: Watch every bar's sales as they happen. The top drink, the busiest bar, and the busiest hour.

steps.title: Restocking
steps.text: Stock is issued to each bar, and confirmed with a PIN. When a bar runs low, a runner gets the alert. The runner collects the drinks, each case tagged with a QR code, and scans them in at the bar.

steps.title: Food stalls
steps.text: Food stalls sell on the same tills, with a kitchen screen if they want one.

steps.title: Drink nudges
steps.text: Send an offer straight to phones. Two for one at the Cocktail Bar, for fifteen minutes. A quiet bar fills up, and a long line clears. Fans opt in, nudges are capped, and late in the night they turn to food, and a safe ride home.

steps.title: The big screens
steps.text: The big screens run from the Event Pal Box, in up to 4K. The DJ, the lineup, shout-outs, and graphics made for your fete. Every graphic is made from your own flyers and promo media, so it all matches your theme. Announcements go up on the big screen too, from set times to last call.

steps.title: Sponsors
steps.text: Sponsors get their slots on a schedule the system keeps. Pause it for the headline act, and it picks back up, with every missed slot worked back in.

steps.title: Crowd battles
steps.text: Then the crowd takes over. Shake to win, left side against right side, VIP against general, with AVA calling it, and the scores on the big screen.

steps.title: Light show
steps.text: On the drop, every phone flashes the same colour. The whole crowd becomes the light show.

steps.title: Votes, shout-outs and photos
steps.text: The crowd votes for the next tune. Birthdays and crews buy a shout-out on the big screen. And the best photos go up in the sponsor's frame.

steps.title: The stream
steps.text: Family abroad can watch too. Sell a stream pass like a ticket, with one device per pass, and no recording for viewers.

steps.title: Help button
steps.text: If someone needs help, one tap sends their spot to security. And at closing, AVA points everyone to a taxi, the last bus, or lost and found.

steps.title: Pal Monitor
steps.text: Run the whole fete from your phone. Gates, bars, stock, sales, and alerts, on Pal Monitor.

steps.title: Your assistant, your eyes
steps.text: Think of AVA as your personal assistant, and your eyes at the event. She watches every gate, every bar and every screen, all night, all at once. She spots a problem before you do, works out why, and tells the right person. And when you need to know something, just ask her. How many are in, which bar's busiest, what's running low. She answers in seconds, so you can enjoy your own fete.

steps.title: AVA watching
steps.text: AVA watches every part of it. If a gate goes offline or a bar runs dry, she looks into it, and messages you on Telegram. Need something done? Just tell her, or have her contact admin.

steps.title: Cash control
steps.text: Every till is covered. Floats, drops, and a blind close. A photo when a drawer opens with no sale. And every outlet's cash, settled.

steps.title: The morning after
steps.text: The morning after, your report's waiting. Tickets by tier and outlet, entries, bar and stall sales, stock, and the nudges that worked. And a crowd energy report, hour by hour, from the shakes, votes and reactions.

steps.title: Next year
steps.text: And AVA keeps your crowd. Everyone who asked about this fete gets the alert when the next one drops.

steps.title: Your fete, your way
steps.text: This was just one way a fete could be configured and managed. It doesn't set how your event should flow, and it's not everything Event Pal can do. Use the parts you need, in the order you want. Your fete, your way, managed by Event Pal.
